description: Language-neutral parity catalog for the WHOLE dispatch (Task 4): the compiled core binary invoked directly vs the BASH FLOOR reached as `PLAINKEEP_CORE=off <vault>/plainkeep <verb> <args...>` — the pre-core dispatcher preserved verbatim inside the shim. test/run_core_parity.py's 'dispatch' comparator builds the fixture vault, gives each side its OWN copy (isolated .logs), installs the floor's pieces (the shim script + bin/lib/guardrail.py next to the copied resolver.py), and compares exit status, stdout, stderr, and the appended gate audit line. A signal death is compared as subprocess's NEGATIVE returncode, so `exec`-style death-by-signal cannot be faked by exiting 128+N. The floor side is additionally handed a LIVE tracer as PLAINKEEP_CORE_BIN and every case asserts the tracer never ran — an ambiguous-mode run is not a gate. Fixture grammar additions over guardrail.json (additive): verbs[].run sets a verb's run.py CONTENT (so a verb can exit 7, print its argv, or kill itself) and the top-level `venv` key writes a fake $PLAINKEEP_HOME/.venv/bin/python3 that is either 'live' (a symlink to the running python3 — CPython then reports sys.executable AS that path, which is how a verb can tell which interpreter was picked) or 'broken' (executable, exits 1 on `-c ''`). Invocation shape: {compare:'dispatch', verb?, args?:[...], home_via_symlink?:bool, expect_stdout_contains?:'...', expect_returncodes?:{core:SPEC, floor:SPEC}, expect_stderr_divergence?:{core_contains:'...', floor:'...'}}. verb omitted means NO argv at all (the default-verb path). expect_stdout_contains adds an absolute assertion on top of the differential so two sides cannot agree on the wrong answer. expect_returncodes replaces the returncode-agreement check with an exact expectation for EACH side — use it both to pin a known divergence and to state an agreement absolutely; a SPEC is a literal returncode or one of the symbolic forms 'signal' (died by the signal named in args[0], resolved on this platform), 'fallback' (survived the re-raise, exited 128+N) or 'sigtrap' (bun's crash handler intercepted the re-raise). expect_stderr_divergence likewise replaces the stderr-agreement check, for the one case where the two sides legitimately differ in what they PRINT. DO NOT author a case whose first argv element is --version, -v, --core-selftest (bare) or --core-resolve/--core-api/--core-gate (any args): the binary answers those ITSELF before dispatch, which is a SANCTIONED divergence from the floor (core prints its identity and exits 0 so the artifact is unambiguously distinguishable — plan-phase1 'Binary introspection flags', advisor B4 — while the floor gates them as unknown verbs, exit 4). The comparator rejects those shapes with that explanation rather than reporting a difference that is correct; assert flag behavior in a bun test or a shim check instead.

cases.name: exit-code-matrix
cases.rationale: Every code in the frozen protocol, each reached the way it is actually reached in production: 0 from a read verb that ran; 2 from the VERB'S OWN usage error inside run.py (not the gate — the dispatcher must pass a child's 2 through untouched); 3 from the gate refusing a confirm verb, and 0 once --yes clears it; 5 from a deny verb; 4 twice over, once from the gate's unknown-verb path (with the did-you-mean line the floor prints) and once from the dispatcher's own 'has no run.py' line (byte-exact vs floor line 40) for a verb that resolves from its cmd.json but ships no script. Far-miss included so the help-hint branch is compared too.

cases.name: argv-forwarding-and-child-status
cases.rationale: What the dispatcher owes the child and what it owes the caller. Forwarding: the verb prints its own sys.argv[1:] as JSON, so an empty arg, an arg with spaces, non-ASCII, an astral emoji, a leading-dash arg and a bare `--` are all proven to arrive positionally intact through both dispatchers (the gate sees the same args, so the audit line's naive space-join is compared too). Status: a child exiting 7 must pass through as 7 (not collapsed to 1), and a child that kills itself with SIGTERM must leave the DISPATCHER dead by that signal — the floor `exec`s the verb, so its wait status is WIFSIGNALED, and a binary that merely exits 143 would differ here (subprocess reports -15 vs 143).

verbs.run:
import os, signal, sys
sys.stdout.write('dying by signal\n')
sys.stdout.flush()
os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGTERM)

cases.name: signal-passthrough-matrix
cases.rationale: One invocation for every signal that (a) terminates by default and (b) exists on BOTH macOS and Linux, since this catalog must run on either — each carrying an explicit expectation of what BOTH sides must produce. That boundary is stated rather than implied: the one default-terminating signal it leaves out is SIGEMT (macOS 7), because Python's signal module has no SIGEMT on Linux; it was measured AGREEING on macOS and is recorded in .orchestrate/raw/task4-fix2-signal-matrix.log rather than guarded here. Names resolve per platform on purpose, so a cell means the same SIGNAL rather than the same number. Partial coverage is what let two separate defect classes hide here — first bun's Linux signal NAMES (fixed in a9eb69a), then bun's signal DELIVERY (found by spec re-review r2 because no case exercised the numbers involved) — so the enumeration is now the whole set rather than a sample, and every cell is a named case that reddens if delivery moves in EITHER direction, including toward correctness. The verb restores SIG_DFL for the named signal and kills itself. Cells: 'signal' = died by that signal (-N, resolved per platform since SIGBUS is 10 on macOS and 7 on Linux); 'sigtrap' = bun's crash handler intercepted the re-raise and killed the dispatcher with SIGTRAP instead; 'fallback' = bun ignores that signal process-wide, so the re-raise is a no-op and the dispatcher exits 128+N. Measured on bun 1.3.14 / macOS arm64 (.orchestrate/raw/task4-fix2-signal-matrix.log): 15 signals reproduce the floor exactly; 6 diverge — SIGILL/SIGFPE/SIGBUS/SIGSEGV die as SIGTRAP, SIGPIPE/SIGXFSZ take the 128+N fallback. The four fault cells pin a SECOND facet that a returncode table cannot see and that this exhaustive sweep surfaced: bun's crash handler also prints a crash report to stderr where the floor is silent, so those cells assert the core's stderr carries it AND the floor's is empty. Excluded on purpose: the stop/continue family (SIGSTOP, SIGTSTP, SIGCONT, SIGTTIN, SIGTTOU), which suspends rather than kills and would hang the harness, and the ignored-by-default set (SIGURG, SIGCHLD, SIGIO, SIGWINCH, SIGINFO), where the child simply exits 0. WHEN A DIVERGENCE CELL GOES RED: bun now delivers that signal — flip the cell to {'core':'signal','floor':'signal'} and delete the matching paragraph in dispatch.ts.

verbs.run:
import os, signal, sys
name = sys.argv[1]
sig = getattr(signal, name)
try:
    signal.signal(sig, signal.SIG_DFL)
except (OSError, ValueError):
    pass  # SIGKILL cannot have its disposition set; it kills regardless
sys.stdout.write('dying by ' + name + '\n')
sys.stdout.flush()
os.kill(os.getpid(), sig)

cases.name: default-verb-and-help-alias
cases.rationale: The floor's argv preamble, which is easy to get subtly wrong: `VERB="${1:-help}"` substitutes on unset OR EMPTY (so `plainkeep ''` is `help`, and the empty string is consumed by the shift rather than forwarded), and the `-h|--help -> help` rewrite happens AFTER the shift so the remaining args survive. The fixture ships a real `help` verb printing its own argv, so each of these DISPATCHES rather than 404ing and the forwarded args are visible in stdout.

verbs.run:
import json, sys
print('helped ' + json.dumps(sys.argv[1:], ensure_ascii=False))

cases.name: interpreter-venv-absent
cases.rationale: The zero-install path: no $PLAINKEEP_HOME/.venv exists, so both dispatchers must run the verb on bare `python3` from PATH. The verb reports which interpreter carried it by comparing sys.executable against $PLAINKEEP_HOME/.venv, and the expected token is asserted absolutely — otherwise two sides agreeing on 'system' would prove nothing about the live-venv case.

verbs.run:
import os, sys
h = os.environ.get('PLAINKEEP_HOME', '')
venv = os.path.join(h, '.venv')
print('venv' if h and sys.executable.startswith(venv) else 'system')

cases.name: interpreter-venv-live
cases.rationale: ADR-008's reason the probe exists at all: when $PLAINKEEP_HOME/.venv/bin/python3 is present AND starts, BOTH dispatchers must prefer it, so `plainkeep index`/`search` see the optional deps with no PATH surgery. Asserted absolutely ('venv'), which is what distinguishes this case from the absent/broken ones.

verbs.run:
import os, sys
h = os.environ.get('PLAINKEEP_HOME', '')
venv = os.path.join(h, '.venv')
print('venv' if h and sys.executable.startswith(venv) else 'system')

cases.name: interpreter-venv-broken
cases.rationale: The failure the `-x`-only check misses and the floor's comments warn about: a .venv/bin/python3 that survived a system-python upgrade or an ABI break is still executable but no longer STARTS, and picking it would return 126/127 on every verb. Both dispatchers must run the `-c ''` probe and fall back to bare python3 — proven absolutely ('system') against the live case's 'venv'.

verbs.run:
import os, sys
h = os.environ.get('PLAINKEEP_HOME', '')
venv = os.path.join(h, '.venv')
print('venv' if h and sys.executable.startswith(venv) else 'system')

cases.name: prototype-named-verbs
cases.rationale: A verb name is a DIRECTORY NAME a pack ships, so it is attacker-shaped, and the dispatcher's interception table is a JS object literal with a prototype. Indexing it as `INTERCEPTS[verb]` resolved an INHERITED member for each of these eight names and treated it as a registered interception: the verb never ran, and for `toString`/`constructor` the binary exited 0 while writing an audit line saying the verb was allowed — an enforcement tool reporting success for work it did not do. Nothing about that is visible to a differential unless a case actually uses such a name, which is why these exist. Each verb's run.py prints a marker, so the assertion is that the REAL verb ran on both sides, not merely that the two sides agreed. `__proto__` is included even though it is the one name that could not silently succeed (it threw, exit 5): it is the same defect class, and a fix that guards only the callable members would pass without it.

cases.name: symlinked-home-not-canonicalized
cases.rationale: The realpath decision (field guide #1), pinned. Both sides are invoked with PLAINKEEP_HOME pointing at a SYMLINK to the vault (the macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp shape), and the verb reports whether the PLAINKEEP_HOME it inherited still differs from its realpath. The dispatcher treats PLAINKEEP_HOME as opaque text and canonicalizes nothing, so the answer must be 'not canonical' on BOTH sides: the value a caller supplied is the value every verb sees. If either side started calling realpath() on it, this case fails — as would every vault whose path runs through a symlink, silently relocating .logs and the resolver's engine bin/ relative to what the operator typed. The basename is compared too (both aliases are named `vault`), since the two sides necessarily live under different temp roots.

verbs.run:
import json, os, sys
h = os.environ.get('PLAINKEEP_HOME', '')
print(json.dumps({'canonical': h == os.path.realpath(h), 'base': os.path.basename(h), 'argv': sys.argv[1:]}))

cases.name: large-output-across-the-pipe-buffer
cases.rationale: A verb whose output exceeds the pipe buffer. This catalog was 213/213 green while the core SILENTLY TRUNCATED any such verb and reported failure, because no case crossed the threshold — the 'green test of nothing' class (quality review r1, Q1). Mechanism: bun marks its own stdout/stderr O_NONBLOCK when they are PIPES, the flag lives on the open file description, and `stdio: "inherit"` hands that same description to the child; CPython then raises BlockingIOError on the first write it cannot satisfy in full. Measured before the fix: `plainkeep <verb> --json | cat` delivered 81,920 bytes and exited 1 where the floor delivered 500,062 and exited 0, byte-identically at face8b7 — i.e. pre-existing since Task 4. The harness captures with pipes, so these three invocations sit exactly on that condition. Each verb writes its BULK FIRST and a short TAIL MARKER LAST, so the assertion is the real outcome — the whole payload arrived — not merely that the two sides agree: a build truncating both sides identically would still fail the marker. v_bigerr's marker goes to STDOUT after the big STDERR write, which is what makes fd 2 checkable through a stdout expectation.

verbs.run:
import sys
sys.stdout.write('o' * 500000)
sys.stderr.write('e' * 500000)
sys.stdout.write('\nBIGBOTH-TAIL\n')
sys.stderr.write('\n')
